Use case: precise-object-edit.
Image 1 is the exact latest Mina dragon edit target. The user points out that the claws/horns at the wing tips do not match on the two sides. Correct ONLY the wing claw anatomy and corresponding tiny tip details, with strict identity preservation.

- Match the number, elegant hooked shape, taper, proportional length, dark base and ivory tip coverage between these two wrist claws. They are a bilateral matched pair seen at different rotations, not unrelated horns.
- The image-right raised wing currently has an extra pale horn/cap along its upper leading ridge above/behind its jeweled wrist, unlike the other wing. The remaining wrist claw is the counterpart of the single claw above the image-left wing's jeweled wrist.

Do not introduce extra claws on one side, random white horns, mismatched white spike caps, or a third wrist claw. Preserve natural perspective; mirrored structure does NOT mean a symmetrical pose.

IMPORTANT: Preserve the asymmetric flying pose exactly: image-right wing raised and image-left wing lower. Do NOT rotate or resize whole wings to make the picture mirror-symmetric. Huge wings remain dominant; their established membranes, broad silhouette and clean continuous frill pattern remain unchanged except the localized erroneous claw areas. Keep every existing navy bow and blue gem in place.

LOCK EVERYTHING ELSE: same face and expression, black fringe, blue eye, head size, small sturdy torso, two arms and two hind legs, complete body pose, black/navy colors and limited white, chest jewel, long flowing tail with the large blue gemstone forming its terminal end, linework and shading, 3:2 composition and transparent-alpha background. Do not modify the tail jewel at all. No new objects, no lettering, no labels. Produce one corrected version of the same image.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Extremely localized removal. Image 1 is the exact edit target. Correct ONE extra claw, changing nothing else.

Everything outside that one removed protrusion must be preserved faithfully: the face, compact body, lower wing, large wing membranes and frill ornaments, all other jewels, long tail and terminal large blue jewel, colors, linework, shading, canvas, pose and framing.
